A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
leisure externalities are important in the determination of growth but that they should be taken together with the other factors that are known to be relevant.

leisure externalities are a powerful tool to generate growth differences, but the model is not able to explain the fact that countries with higher leisure preference and higher leisure externalities have lower education attainment and lower growth.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the inclusion of leisure preference and externality in a two-sector endogenous growth model is important in order to understand differences in growth rates and labor supply across different countries.
